items.stem: Which of the following is a source of heat?

explain.why: Ice is cold. It takes in heat.
Cold milk is not a source of heat.
A cold spoon does not give out heat.

solution: The Sun gives out a lot of heat.

items.stem: Which of the following gives out heat when electricity flows through it?

explain.why: A wooden spoon does not give out heat.
Water does not give out heat when electricity is not used on it.
A rubber ball does not give out heat.

solution: A toaster changes electrical energy into heat.

items.stem: Which instrument is used to measure temperature?

explain.why: A ruler measures length.
A balance measures mass.
A measuring cylinder measures volume.

solution: Temperature is measured with a thermometer.

items.stem: Which of the following is the unit used to measure temperature?

explain.why: Gram is a unit of mass.
Centimetre is a unit of length.
Newton is a unit of force.

solution: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

items.stem: Temperature is a measure of how ____ an object is.

explain.why: Mass tells us how heavy an object is.
Size is not temperature.
Speed is not temperature.

solution: Temperature tells how hot or cold something is.

items.stem: Heat is a form of ____.

explain.why: Heat is not a push or a pull.
Heat has no mass and takes up no space.
Heat is not a material.

solution: Heat is a form of energy.

items.stem: A cup of hot tea is left on a table in a cool room. Which way does heat flow?
options: From the surroundings to the tea
From the table to the tea
From the tea to the surroundings

explain.why: Heat flows from hot to cold.
The tea is hotter than the table.
There is a difference in temperature, so heat flows.

solution: Heat flows from the hotter tea to the cooler surroundings.

items.stem: A large bucket and a small cup both hold water at 50 °C. Which statement is correct?
options: The cup has more heat, and both are at the same temperature
The bucket has more heat, and both are at the same temperature
The bucket is at a higher temperature than the cup
Both have the same heat and the same temperature

explain.why: More water at the same temperature holds more heat.
Both are at 50 °C.
Different amounts of water hold different amounts of heat.

solution: Same temperature, but more water means more heat.

items.stem: A hot metal ball is dropped into a cup of cold water. Which statement is correct?
options: The ball loses heat and the water gains heat
The ball gains heat and the water loses heat
Both the ball and the water gain heat
Both the ball and the water lose heat

explain.why: The ball is the hotter one.
One of them has to lose the heat.
One of them has to gain the heat.

solution: Heat flows from the hot ball to the cold water.

items.stem: Blocks P, Q and R are placed in contact in a row as shown. Which block both gains heat and loses heat?

explain.why: P is the hottest, so it only loses heat.
R is the coolest, so it only gains heat.
Q is cooler than P and hotter than R.

solution: Q gains heat from P and loses heat to R.

items.stem: Mei puts her left hand into hot water and her right hand into cold water for a minute. She then puts both hands into warm water. How do her hands feel?
options: The left hand feels hotter than the right hand
The left hand feels cooler than the right hand
Neither hand can feel the water

explain.why: The left hand was in hotter water, so the warm water feels cooler to it.
Our hands judge by the heat gained or lost.
Both hands can feel it.

solution: Our hands are poor judges of temperature, so we use a thermometer.

items.stem: Why do we use a thermometer instead of our hand to find how hot water is?
options: A thermometer makes the water hotter
Our sense of hot and cold is not exact
Our hand is always colder than the water
Water cannot be felt with the hand

explain.why: A thermometer does not change the water.
This is not always true.
We can feel water. We just cannot measure exactly.

solution: A thermometer gives an exact reading.

items.stem: Which list contains only sources of heat?
options: The Sun, burning wood, an electric stove
The Sun, ice, an electric stove
Burning wood, a refrigerator shelf, the Sun
An electric stove, a snowman, burning wood

explain.why: Ice is not a source of heat.
A refrigerator shelf is not a source of heat.
A snowman is not a source of heat.

solution: The Sun, burning wood and electric stoves all give out heat.

items.stem: Why do our hands become warm when we rub them together?
options: Our hands take in cold from the air
Heat flows from the cold air to our hands

explain.why: Cold is not taken in.
Heat flows from hot to cold.
Mass is not related to heat here.

solution: Rubbing makes friction, which makes heat.

items.stem: A hot metal ball is put into cold water. The graph shows the temperatures of the ball and the water. Which line is for the ball?

explain.why: The ball is the hot object. It starts at 100 °C.
The two lines start at different temperatures.
One of the lines belongs to the ball.

solution: The ball was hotter at the start, so its line starts higher.

options: The bathtub has the higher temperature because it holds more heat in it

The two have the same heat if they feel equally warm

explain.why: Heat and temperature are different things.
The bathtub has much more water.
Feeling is not a measure of heat.

solution: Temperature tells how hot. The amount of heat also depends on how much water there is.

D: The temperature of the coffee falls.

explain.why: C is wrong because the table is colder than the coffee.
C is wrong because the table is colder than the coffee.

solution: Heat flows from the coffee to the table, so the coffee cools.

solution: The liquid is at the second mark above 30, so 34 °C.

The soup cools down and the water warms up

explain.why: Heat flows from the hot soup to the cold water.
Heat is not made. It flows.
They have different temperatures, so heat flows.

solution: The soup loses heat and the water gains heat.

items.stem: Which of the following can be used to find out how hot an object is?

explain.why: A balance measures mass.
A stopwatch measures time.
A tape measures length.

solution: A thermometer measures temperature.

options: Heat flows from the block to the water
Heat flows from the water to the block
The block makes the water hotter

explain.why: There is no difference in temperature.
There is no difference in temperature.
No heat flows between objects at the same temperature.

solution: There is no temperature difference, so no heat flows.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a source of heat?

An electric iron gives out heat.
The Sun gives out heat.

solution: Ice takes in heat. It is not a source.

They already matched from 8 minutes.

solution: The lines meet at 8 minutes.

items.stem: A cook says, "The soup is full of heat, so its temperature must be very high." Which reply is best?
options: Not always, as a big pot of warm soup can hold more heat
Yes: heat and temperature are the same thing, so it is very hot
Yes: temperature measures the amount of heat in the soup
No: soup has no heat at all, only temperature

explain.why: Heat and temperature are different.
Temperature tells how hot, not how much heat.
Soup has heat.

solution: Temperature and the amount of heat are different.

items.stem: Hot water at 80 °C is put in a cup. A cold metal spoon at 20 °C is placed in it. Which graph is most likely for the temperature of the spoon?
options: A line that falls, then levels off at a lower value
A line that rises above 80 °C and keeps rising
A line that rises, then levels off below 80 °C

explain.why: The spoon gains heat, so it warms.
The spoon gains heat.
The spoon cannot become hotter than the water.

solution: The spoon warms up until it matches the water.

items.stem: Which is the most suitable way to measure the temperature of boiling water?
options: A thermometer that reads from -10 to 50 °C

explain.why: The liquid would rise beyond the top of the scale.
This is unsafe and gives no number.
A stopwatch measures time.

solution: The scale must go above 100 °C.

items.stem: Three identical cups with hot water at 90 °C are left in a room at 25 °C. The table shows the temperature after 30 minutes. Which cup lost the most heat?
options: They all lost the same amount

explain.why: The water in P cooled the least.
The water in Q cooled less than in R.
The final temperatures are different.

solution: R fell the most, from 90 to 41.

items.stem: In the same table, which cup will the water in the room gain the most heat from?

explain.why: P gave out the least heat.
Q gave out less than R.
The cups gave out different amounts.

solution: R lost the most heat, so the room gained the most from R.

items.stem: Which of the following shows that temperature and heat are different?
options: Two beakers with the same temperature always feel exactly the same to touch
A thermometer reading rises when we add ice cubes to hot water
Hot water always contains less heat than cold water of any amount
Beakers at 60 °C with 100 ml and 500 ml give out different amounts of heat

explain.why: Feeling does not show the amount of heat.
Ice makes it fall.
The amount depends on both temperature and amount of water.

solution: The bigger beaker gives out more heat, though both start at the same temperature.

items.stem: A hot iron block is dropped into cold water. Which statement describes what happens to the heat?
options: The iron loses heat and the heat disappears
The water makes heat to match the iron
The heat lost by the iron is gained by the water
The iron gains heat from the water

explain.why: The heat does not disappear. It flows to the water.
Water does not make heat.
The iron is hotter, so it loses heat.

solution: Heat moves from the iron to the water.

items.stem: A thermometer is moved from a cup of ice water into a cup of hot water. Which describes how the reading changes?
options: It jumps to the final reading as soon as it is put in
It rises fast at first, then slowly until steady
It falls first and then rises to the final reading

explain.why: Heat takes time to flow into the thermometer.
The thermometer only gains heat.
It gains heat from the hot water.

solution: The thermometer gains heat, and its reading rises until it matches the water.

items.stem: Two metal blocks of the same size, P at 100 °C and Q at 0 °C, are placed in contact. After a long time, which temperature is the most likely for both blocks?

explain.why: P loses heat, so both cannot be 100 °C.
Q gains heat, so both cannot be 0 °C.
They cannot be hotter than P was.

solution: Equal metal blocks meet halfway between the two temperatures.

items.stem: Which of the following can we measure directly with a thermometer?
options: How much heat the tea contains
How much heat the tea will give to the room
How hot a cup of tea is

explain.why: A thermometer measures temperature, not the amount of heat.
A thermometer does not measure the amount of heat.
A thermometer does not measure mass.

solution: A thermometer measures temperature.

items.stem: An ice cube is put into a cup of warm water. Which statement about the temperature of the water is correct?
options: It rises because the ice gives heat to the water
It stays the same because ice has no heat
It falls because the water gives heat to the ice
It falls because the ice gives coldness to the water

explain.why: Ice is colder than the water.
The ice is colder, so heat flows to it.
Heat flows from water to ice. Cold is not given.

solution: Heat flows from the warm water to the ice.

items.stem: Aisha reads the thermometer in hot water as 78 °C and later reads 52 °C. Which is the best description of her results?
options: The water gained heat and its temperature fell by 26 °C
The water lost heat and its temperature fell by 26 °C
The water lost heat and its temperature fell by 130 °C
The water lost heat and its temperature rose by 26 °C

explain.why: A falling temperature means heat was lost.
Subtract, do not add.
The temperature fell.

solution: 78 - 52 = 26 °C. Falling temperature means heat was lost.

items.stem: A hot-water pipe passes through a cold room. Which statement is correct?
options: Heat flows from the pipe to the room, so the pipe loses heat
Heat flows from the room to the pipe
No heat flows because the pipe is metal
The room makes the pipe cooler by giving cold to it

explain.why: The pipe is hotter than the room.
Heat flows whenever temperatures differ.
Heat flows. Cold does not flow.

solution: Heat flows from the hotter pipe to the cooler room.
